chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Zur'a, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about two men who had a slave girl between them, so they married her to a man. Then a man bought part of their shares. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes prohibited to him by his purchase of her, and that is that her sale is her divorce, unless he buys her from all of them entirely.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect on a slave girl's marriage when one of her co-owners buys his share?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the principle of *tamleek* (granting ownership) in the context of joint slave ownership, where purchasing a share effectively severs the marital bond for that specific co-owner. It highlights the juristic nuance that the sale of a slave girl is legally equivalent to her divorce (*talaq*) for the seller, a concept rooted in the practical realities of early Islamic society. The ruling underscores the necessity of complete acquisition to maintain the marital status, reflecting the detailed fiqh development in Shia jurisprudence regarding concubinage and marriage contracts.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about two men who had a slave girl between them, so they got her married to a man. Then the man bought part of their shares. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is Prohibited unto him by his stipulation of her, and that is that her sale is her divorce, unless he buys her from them entirely’.
